sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Cylindropuntia leptocaulis is a shrubby cactus of the south-western United States and northern Mexico, about 0.6–1.5 m tall. Its cylindrical branch segments are slender. It grows in desert scrub, dry grassland and chaparral.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The greenish-yellow flowers reach about 2.5 cm; small red fruits, about 1.3 cm long, often persist through winter. Fruits have been traditionally eaten after removing the glochids, the small barbed bristles. The plate shows the slender branches, flowers and red fruits. Compared with C. bigelovii, its segments are thinner and its fruits remain coloured.
